title: Specification
description: A FRETISH specification, optionally annotated with fitness metadata produced by the PEREDUR repair tool.

modes.description: Operating modes a requirement's scope may be relative to. Their own namespace, disjoint from in_atoms and out_atoms; they join the environment (uncontrollable) side of the synthesis partition. Absent means the specification uses no scopes.

Requirement.description: A single FRETISH requirement with condition, condition-type, response, and timing.

condition.description: Propositional formula that activates the requirement.

condition-type.description: Whether the condition activates on a rising edge (trigger) or at every timepoint it holds (continual).

response.description: Propositional formula that must hold when the condition activates.

weakenable.description: When false, the genetic algorithm never mutates this requirement or uses it as a crossover source. Defaults to true when absent.

Scope.description: The interval, relative to when a mode holds, over which the requirement is enforced. Absent means Global, which is also what an omitted FRET scope means.

mode.description: Name of the mode, which must appear in the specification's modes list. Required for every type but Global, and forbidden for Global.

Timing.description: Temporal modifier controlling when the response must hold relative to the condition.

ticks.description: Tick bound; required for WithinTicks, ForTicks, and AfterTicks.

stop.description: Propositional stop condition; required for Until and Before.

ComponentScore.description: Score and weight for one fitness component.

name.description: Identifier of the fitness component (e.g. syntactic, semantic, status).

score.description: Raw score in [0, 1] produced by this component.

weight.description: Relative weight used when computing the weighted average.

FitnessRecord.description: Fitness breakdown produced by the PEREDUR repair tool. Present only on output files, never required on input.

total.description: Weighted average of all component scores, in [0, 1].
